proposals.before: The emperor repented and said, "This is what comes of heeding my own counsel!"
proposals.after: The emperor repented and said, "This is what comes of heeding that counsel!"
proposals.reason: Chinese 用言 refers to following Han's advice just given, not the emperor's own counsel.

proposals.before: Prince Shou'an used Dili's stratagem to lure Chagai out and kill him; not one of those who had been coerced was harmed, and that was entirely Dili's doing.
proposals.after: Prince Shou'an used Dilie's stratagem to lure Chagai out and kill him; not one of those who had been coerced was harmed, and that was entirely Dilie's doing.
proposals.reason: English shortens 敵獵 to Dili; the established spelling elsewhere is Dilie.

proposals.before: Prince Shou'an used Dili's plan to lure and kill Chagai; of all who had been coerced, not one was harmed—it was all Dili's doing.
proposals.after: Prince Shou'an used Dilie's plan to lure and kill Chagai; of all who had been coerced, not one was harmed—it was all Dilie's doing.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise misspells Dilie as Dili.

proposals.before: In the autumn of the ninth year Ge married his son to Chongyuan; Ge took part in the conspiracy and was executed by dismemberment.
proposals.after: In the autumn of the ninth year Ge made his son Chongyuan's son-in-law; Ge took part in the conspiracy and was executed by dismemberment.
proposals.reason: Chinese 為重元婿 means made his son Chongyuan's son-in-law, not that Ge married his son to Chongyuan himself.

decisions.reason: In 此吾用言之過至此, 吾用言 is the emperor's fault in heeding advice; s0011 帝從其言 shows that counsel was another's, so "my own counsel" wrongly makes the advice his invention, and "heeding that counsel" restores the sense.
Source 敵獵 is Dilie in the surrounding units (s0157, s0161); "Dili" is an inconsistent truncation of the same name, and Dilie corrects the spelling without changing the rest of the idiomatic sense.
The literal field has the same truncated spelling of 敵獵 as Dili; Dilie matches the Chinese name used in this unit and adjacent context.

革以其子為重元婿 means Ge made his son Chongyuan's 婿 (son-in-law), not that he married his son to Chongyuan; the proposed wording corrects that kinship error while leaving the conspiracy and execution clauses intact.
